narrative:
The model predicts a 16% chance that you will fail your final year, which indicates a concerning risk of not passing. This prediction is based on several factors that have been shown to influence student outcomes.

The most significant factor is your number of school absences, which is notably higher than the average of just under four absences among students who passed. Frequent absences can disrupt your learning and understanding of the material, making it harder to keep up with your studies. 

Another important aspect is your desire for higher education. While this is a positive indicator, it alone does not guarantee success. It suggests motivation, but without consistent study habits and attendance, that motivation may not translate into academic performance.

Lastly, your history of past failures is a strong indicator of future performance. Although you have not failed any classes before, the model considers the overall context of students who have struggled in the past. This context can weigh heavily on predictions, especially if combined with other risk factors like absences.

To improve your academic performance, consider increasing your study time and ensuring you attend all classes. Engaging in extra educational support or tutoring could also be beneficial. Additionally, maintaining a consistent routine and seeking help when needed can help you stay on track and enhance your chances of passing.
